one_liner: C++ AI-native search database for RAG; vendor run shows 10x Elasticsearch's full-text QPS on 33M Wikipedia documents.
what_it_does: Infinity is a standalone database server for hybrid retrieval: BM25 full-text, dense vectors, sparse vectors and tensor (multi-vector) search plus structured filters, fused with RRF, weighted-sum or ColBERT rerankers. Clients talk to it through a Python SDK over Thrift (port 23817), an HTTP API, a PostgreSQL-wire port for a SQL subset, or an embedded Python module. It is not a drop-in for Elasticsearch: tables have typed schemas and queries are built with SDK calls such as match_text and match_dense, not the Elasticsearch query DSL.
how_it_is_fast: Full-text search runs over its own inverted index with block-max WAND (blockmax_wand_iterator), a batch OR iterator and a BM25 ranker, so top-k OR queries skip posting blocks whose maximum score cannot enter the heap. Dense search uses HNSW graphs whose vectors can be stored with LVQ (locally-adaptive 8-bit scalar quantization) or RaBitQ, scored with runtime-dispatched SIMD int8 and float L2/IP kernels (HNSW_I8L2_64 and similar). The server is C++23 with modules, built at -O3 in Release.
when_to_use: RAG retrieval that needs BM25, dense and sparse vector search and reranking in one engine on one machine, for example behind RAGFlow.
High-QPS top-10 keyword OR queries over tens of millions of short documents, where Elasticsearch's memory footprint matters (10.0 GB vs 21.0 GB in the vendor Enwiki run).
Million-scale ANN search where recall around 0.95-0.97 at top-100 is acceptable in exchange for 7-17x the QPS of Elasticsearch 8.13 in the vendor run.
Python-first stacks that want a single-binary server or an embedded Python module instead of a JVM cluster.
when_not_to_use: When top-100 recall must exceed about 0.98 on SIFT-like data: Elasticsearch reached 0.992 and Qdrant 0.979 against Infinity's 0.973 with its LVQ-quantised index.
When index build time or disk footprint dominate: Qdrant built SIFT1M in 46 s vs 74 s and GIST1M in 366 s vs 463 s, and used 418 MB vs 792 MB of disk on SIFT1M.

Write-heavy concurrent DELETE plus INSERT ingestion: open issue #3418 (v0.7.0-dev5) reports a delete-conflict livelock, compaction replaying one timestamp for hours with memory growing from 8.5 to 14.8 GiB, and leaked sessions exhausting connections.
When you need Elasticsearch API compatibility, aggregations or a multi-node cluster; none is described in the README.
On x86-64 CPUs without AVX2 (the README requires it), or when you want a C++ library to link rather than a server to operate.

integration.form: server binary (Docker image infiniflow/infinity or standalone) with Python, HTTP and PostgreSQL-wire clients; embedded Python module
integration.dependencies: building from source needs vcpkg packages including Abseil, Arrow/Parquet, Boost.Asio, RocksDB, Thrift, oatpp, simdjson, re2, CRoaring, pcre2, spdlog and OpenSSL; client side needs Python 3.11+ and infinity-sdk
integration.min_toolchain: Clang 20+, CMake 4.0.3+, Ninja, C++23 with modules and import std (to build the server); Python 3.11+ for the SDK
integration.platforms: x86-64 with AVX2 on Linux (glibc 2.17+), macOS, Windows 10+ via WSL/WSL2; ARM64 builds go through SIMDe
integration.thread_safety: The server serves many concurrent clients (connection_pool_size 128 by default); the benchmark code notes the SDK socket is unsafe to share between workers, so open one connection per process or thread.

gotchas: Harness flaw: the checked-in recall code compares results against expected_result[i][1:], dropping each query's true nearest neighbour and capping top-100 recall at 0.99, and it cannot score Elasticsearch's vector results at all (they are (id, score) tuples, so `x >> 32` raises a TypeError). Elasticsearch's published 0.992 is above that cap, qdrant_gist.json has no ground_truth_path, and there is no elasticsearch_gist.json, so run.py refuses an Elasticsearch GIST run; the recall column and the Elasticsearch GIST row cannot be reproduced from the repo.

Harness asymmetry on Enwiki: the Elasticsearch client sends a plain match query without `_source` filtering or track_total_hits:false, so every response carries the full source of 10 documents and Elasticsearch counts hits up to its default 10,000 before pruning, while the Infinity client asks only for _row_id and _score over Thrift; Elasticsearch is configured with 5 shards and all 16 Python client processes share the 16-vCPU host with the server.

The QPS mode replays random queries from the 100,000-query set for 30 minutes, so each query repeats about 250 times at Infinity's rate; Infinity has a result_cache option (off in conf/infinity_conf.toml) and the Elasticsearch config disables its request cache, so check the cache setting of the image you benchmark.

Operational bugs open as of 2026-10: WAL files are never recycled because WalFile::RecycleWalFile is commented out (#3435, 54,000 files on one instance, and manual cleanup segfaulted on restart), WAL replay crashes in InitPhase2 (#3497), and an unrecovered append aborts the server (#3434); a block-max WAND crash on queries with 15+ terms was fixed only on 2026-09-21.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Infinity over Manticore Search, the other server-style sibling that beats Elasticsearch, when you need dense, sparse and tensor vector search fused with BM25 in one engine for RAG; pick Tantivy, SeekStorm or PISA when you want an embeddable search library with independent search-benchmark-game numbers rather than a server measured only by its vendor.
verified_claims_summary: The Infinity team ran its own Python driver on one Intel Core i5-13500H (16 vCPU, 32 GB, OpenSUSE Tumbleweed) with every engine in Docker (Elasticsearch 8.13.4 with a 32 GB max heap, Qdrant 1.9.2, Quickwit 0.8.1, Infinity labelled v0.2.0 but started from the floating nightly image): 13,731 vs 1,340 QPS (10.2x) and 1.37 vs 14.75 ms P95 for 100,000 top-10 OR queries on 33M Enwiki documents, 16,320 vs 934 (Elasticsearch) and 1,303 (Qdrant) QPS on SIFT1M top-100 at lower recall (0.973 vs 0.992 and 0.979, LVQ 8-bit vs float32), and 2,200 vs 305 and 339 QPS on GIST1M. No compiler flags are given for any engine, and the harness flaws listed under gotchas mean the recall column is not reproducible from the repo.
status_note: Actively developed (last commit 2026-09-23, SDK 0.7.3), Apache-2.0, about 4.7k stars with 98 open issues including a stream of September 2026 SDK and WAL crash reports; usable as a server for RAG workloads, not as a library to vendor.
